summary: Edeltraud Harzer works in Indology and philosophy. She studied at Charles University, the University of Washington (PhD), and under traditional teachers Sri Narayana Mishra and Ram Shankar Bhattacharya. She held posts at Washington, Puget Sound, Stanford, Indiana, and Texas at Austin.

Edgar Howard Sturtevant was a linguist who studied at Illinois College, Indiana University, and the University of Chicago under Carl Darling Buck. His career included teaching posts at Indiana, Maryville, Missouri, Columbia (1907–1920), and Yale University (1923–1943).

Edgar Polomé worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the Université libre de Bruxelles, Université catholique de Louvain, and KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte. He held posts at the University of Lubumbashi (1956–1960) and the University of Texas at Austin (1961–1997).

Edgar Thurston worked in Indology and history/archaeology after studying at Eton College and King's College London. He served as Superintendent of the Government Museum, Chennai (1885–1908), lecturer at Madras Medical College, and Superintendent of Ethnography for Madras Presidency (1901).

Edgard Blochet was a scholar of Iranian/Central Asian and religious studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and INALCO under James Darmesteter, later teaching at EPHE (1895–1901) and working at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1895–1935).

Edith Frances Claflin worked in linguistics and Indology. She studied at Radcliffe College and Bryn Mawr College, later serving as head of the Greek Department at Choate Rosemary Hall (1916–1933) and lecturer at Barnard College (1936–1945).
Edith Ludowyk-Gyömrői worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at the University of Ceylon, where she studied under G. P. Malalasekera from around 1939 to 1944.

Edith Tóth was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and historian/archaeologist. She studied under Lajos Ligeti, János Harmatta, and László Gaál. From circa 1956 to 1965, she served as Keeper of the Indian collection at the Ferenc Hopp Museum of Asiatic Arts.

Edith Wyschogrod was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. She earned her degrees from Hunter College and Columbia University, later serving as the J. Newton Rayzor Professor of Philosophy and Religious Thought at Rice University from 1992 to 2002.
Edmond Yee works in religious studies and sinology. He held faculty posts attested in 2003 at both Pacific Lutheran Theological Seminary and the Graduate Theological Union.
Edmund Charles Cox was a historian and archaeologist who completed his education at Marlborough College (~1869–1874) and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1874–1877).

Edmund Hardy worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Mainz, Berlin, Heidelberg (under Kuno Fischer), and Freiburg. He held professorial posts at Freiburg, Fribourg (1894–1898), and Würzburg (~1893–1904).

Edmund Henderson Hunt was active in history/archaeology and Indology. Educated at Harrow School and Balliol College, Oxford, he served as Chief Medical Officer for the Nizam's Guaranteed State Railway from circa 1903 to 1931.

Philosopher Edmund Husserl studied at Leipzig (under Wilhelm Wundt), Berlin, Vienna, and Halle. He held academic posts at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1887–1901), the University of Göttingen (1901–1916), and the University of Freiburg (1916–1928).
Edmund Kleinhans was a linguist. He pursued his studies at the University of Innsbruck under Friedrich Stolz and at the University of Leipzig (1892–1893) under Karl Brugmann.

Edmund Leach worked in religious studies and anthropology. He studied at Clare College, King's College, Cambridge, and the LSE under Malinowski and Radcliffe-Brown. He held posts at the LSE (1947–1953), Cambridge (1953–1978), and King's College, Cambridge (1966–1979).

Edmund Martin Küttler worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Vienna under Leopold von Schroeder, Berlin under Josef Strzygowski, and Graz under Rudolf Meringer. He taught at Masaryk University (1927) and directed the Moravian Museum (~1939–1945).

Edmund Nathaniel Snyder was an Indologist who studied at Harvard, Berlin (under Albrecht Weber and Hermann Oldenberg), and Leipzig. He taught Latin at Vassar College (1890) and served as Professor of German and French at University School.
Edmund Stengel studied under Nikolaus Delius and Friedrich Christian Diez from circa 1864 to 1868.

Edmund W. Smith worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He served as Assistant Archaeological Surveyor for the North-West Provinces and Oudh with the Archaeological Survey of India (1886) and became Curator at the State Museum, Lucknow (1898).
